answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a summit as the anchor of the cost.
